author: P. L. King
title: Kevin Kiley criticizes Newsom's fiscal management and announces gas tax legislation - NE Sacramento News
text:
Kevin Kiley, U.S. Congressman representing California’s 3rd district since 2023, has used his social media platform to criticize Governor Gavin Newsom’s handling of state finances and policy decisions in a series of posts on February 10, 2026.
In a post published at 02:58 UTC, Kiley questioned the accuracy of claims made by Governor Newsom regarding fraud prevention efforts: “Newsom is now saying I shouldn’t criticize him for California’s rampant fraud because he “stopped” $125 billion in fraud. This is a made-up number. What is not made-up is the tens of billions that independent audits have found he squandered.”
Later that day, at 18:06 UTC, Kiley commented on reports about Mark Zuckerberg leaving California and linked this departure to state fiscal policies: “Now Zuckerberg is leaving California too. Newsom’s disastrous policies and the proposed ‘wealth tax’ are driving away our citizens and tax dollars. The state’s finances are a house of cards on the brink of collapse.”
At 21:08 UTC, Kiley announced new legislative action aimed at reducing fuel costs for Californians: “Californians pay the highest gas tax yet drive over the deepest potholes. I am introducing the Gas Tax Reduction Act to place a national limit on state gas taxes. The bill will immediately save California drivers 21 cents per gallon.”
Kiley has served in Congress since replacing John Garamendi in 2023 and previously held office in the California State Assembly from 2016 to 2022. Born in Sacramento in 1985 and currently residing in Rocklin, Kiley holds degrees from Harvard University (BA) and Yale University (JD).
